reviews.text: Since they switched to an appointment system, the waiting time has been reduced. It's a bit far, but I feel at ease because the doctor is trustworthy.

The clinic appears to have been renovated, and now has a large, bright examination room with a large window facing the street. I treated a former stray cat, and Dr. Ikeda has a lot of experience, and he suggested various possibilities based on the symptoms, which gave me peace of mind. In fact, the symptoms that had not improved at other hospitals were completely improved.

I took my cat to the vet for a heart condition, but even though this condition requires long-term medication, I was only given a 7-day supply without any explanation.

Ultimately, the condition relapsed immediately, and my cat cried constantly in pain, even losing its voice.

I wish they had properly explained the situation and given me enough medication in one go; I don't think it would have come to this.

Of course, the expenses also increased with each visit.

The head veterinarian's surgical skills are certainly reliable.
However, their internal medicine treatments sometimes involve what seems like over-prescription, relying on multiple medications to potentially cure the condition.
There have been instances where the condition worsened due to the overlapping administration of antibiotics and steroids.
Furthermore, unlike other clinics, they don't explain the necessary tests and costs to the owner before making a decision, perhaps because they primarily rely on insurance. The treatment and consultation fees are quite high.
Previously, the deputy head veterinarian told me, "If you get insurance, we'll make sure it's covered by insurance."
I'm not sure what he meant by that statement.

This family-run clinic has a solid reputation for the director's surgical experience and skill! I regularly have my elderly toy poodle examined here, and since he started treating me, he's regained his energy, which I'm very grateful for! However, the prices are not exactly cheap.
